en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled *Aparimitāyus*:
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty monks, and many others.
[1] Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:
"Mañjuśrī, there exists above [this world] a world-system named Aparimitaguṇasaṃcaya; therein dwells a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja."
For thus he remains, stays, and maintains himself, and he teaches the Dharma to sentient beings.
Listen, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: these humans of Jambudvīpa have short lifespans, living for only a hundred years.

Many untimely deaths have been described for them. However, Mañjuśrī, those beings who shall write down or cause to be written this Dharma discourse called "The Proclamation of the Qualities and Praises of the Tathāgata Aparimitāyus," or who shall hear even its mere name,

or who, having made it into a book, shall keep it in their home, read it, and honor it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, bells, and flags— [for all these, there will be no untimely death].
They shall worship him on all sides with offerings, and those whose lifespans have been exhausted shall once again come to have a lifespan of one hundred years.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, for those beings who hear, retain, or recite the one hundred and eight names of that Tathāgata Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja, their lifespan shall increase.

Those beings whose lifespan is exhausted who hear, retain, or recite this name— their lifespan shall also increase. Therefore, Mañjuśrī, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who desire long life and who hear, write, or cause to be written the one hundred and eight names of that Tathāgata Aparimitāyus will possess these qualities and benefits.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja.
It is thus:
Oṃ, merit, great merit, immeasurable merit, you who have accumulated the equipment of immeasurable life, merit, and wisdom!

Oṃ, O nature of phenomena which is utterly pure in all conditioned things, arisen like the sky, pure by its own nature, surrounded by the Great Vehicle, svāhā! [5] Mañjuśrī, those who write this hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata, or cause them to be written, or having made them into a book, keep them in their home or recite them—
even those whose lifespan is exhausted shall once again have a lifespan of a hundred years.
Having passed away from here, they will be reborn in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Aparimitāyus,
and they will possess immeasurable lifespans in the world-system Aparimitaguṇasaṃcaya. [6] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, ninety-nine billion Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
[7] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, eighty-four billion Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra: [8]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [and so forth, as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, seventy-seven koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
[9] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [and so forth, as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, sixty-five million Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
[10] *Oṃ namo bhagavate* [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, five hundred and fifty million Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra: [11]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5].
At that time, moreover, forty-five koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra:
[12] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, thirty-six billion Buddhas, with one mind and in one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
[13] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, twenty-five billion Buddhas, with one mind and in one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra: [14]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Furthermore, at that time, ten million buddhas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
[15] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].

[As in paragraph 5: Whoever shall write or cause to be written this *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*, even if their lifespan has already expired, they shall attain a lifespan of one hundred years, or else their lifespan shall increase further.
[16] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].

Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra will never be reborn in the hells, nor in the animal realm, nor in the world of Yama, nor ever in the inopportune states (akṣaṇas).
In whatever birth they may be reborn, in every such birth they will remember their past lives. [17]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5].
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, by them eighty-four thousand aggregates of the Dharma (dharmaskandha) will have been caused to be written.
[18] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5].
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, by them eighty-four thousand stūpas for the Dharma King shall have been caused to be built and established.
[19] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, his fivefold obstructions of karma resulting from the five acts of immediate retribution shall go to complete destruction. [20]
[Paragraph 21 is missing in the Sanskrit text.
Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5]. Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra,

Neither Māra, nor those belonging to Māra’s host, nor yakṣas, nor rākṣasas, nor untimely death shall find an opportunity to overcome him. [22] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5]. Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra,
At the time of his death, ninety-nine billion Buddhas will appear before him face-to-face;
a thousand Buddhas will place their hands upon his hand,
and he will pass from Buddha-field to Buddha-field.
One should not give rise to self-doubt, hesitation, or misapprehension.
[23] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5]. Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra,
The four great kings will follow closely behind him, providing protection, shelter, and defense. [24] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Whoever writes this *Aparimitāyur-jñāna-sūtra* or causes it to be written shall be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī, the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitābha. [25]

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [and so forth, as in paragraph 5]. In whatever place on earth they shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyur-sūtra, that place shall become like a caitya and worthy of veneration.
Those animals and birds belonging to the animal realm into whose ears this shall fall will all attain full awakening in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
[26] Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus-sūtra, for them the state of being female shall never again occur. [27]

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5]. Whoever, for the sake of this *Aparimitāyus Sūtra*, this discourse on the Dharma, shall give even a single *kārṣāpaṇa* coin as a gift, by that person a gift is given equal to filling the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system with the seven precious jewels. [28]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5]. Whoever shall worship this Dharma-preacher, by him the entire, complete True Dharma is worshipped. [29]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [and so forth, as in paragraph 5].

Just as it might be possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit from having performed offerings consisting of the seven precious gems for the Tathāgatas such as Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and Śākyamuni, [so too for this...].
But it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit of the *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*.
[30] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].

Suppose one were to make a heap of jewels equal in size to Sumeru, the king of mountains, and give it as a gift; [the merit of this would not approach even a fraction of the merit of the *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*].
It is possible to calculate the measure of that mass of merit,
but it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit of the *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*.
[31] Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].
Just as it might be possible to count every single drop of water if the four great oceans were filled with water,
it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit from the *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*. [32]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as paragraph 5].

Whoever shall write this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, or cause it to be written, and having prepared it, shall worship it, by that person all the Tathāgatas in all the Buddha-fields in the ten directions will have been saluted and worshipped. [33]
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One [and so forth, as in paragraph 5].
The Buddha has arisen through the power of giving; the lions among men have attained the power of giving.
And the sound of the power of giving is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. [34]
The Buddha has arisen through the power of ethical discipline; the lions among men have attained the power of ethical discipline.
And the sound of the power of ethical discipline is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city.
The Buddha has arisen through the power of patience; the lions among men have attained the power of patience.
And the sound of the power of patience is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city.
[36] The Buddha has arisen through the power of vigor; the lions among men have attained the power of vigor.
And the sound of the power of vigor is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. [37]
The Buddha has arisen through the power of meditative concentration; the lions among men have attained the power of meditative concentration.
And the sound of the power of meditative concentration is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city.
[38] The Buddha has arisen through the power of wisdom; the lions among men have attained the power of wisdom.
And the sound of the power of wisdom is heard as he enters the city of the Compassionate One. Om, homage to the Blessed One [etc., as in paragraph 5].

The Blessed One having spoken thus, the monks, those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, and that entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—were uplifted in mind by the Blessed One’s words.
[He] rejoiced in what was spoken. [40]
